description: The full data science workflow on real datasets: collecting and cleaning data, warehousing and business intelligence, visualisation, machine learning for clustering, dimensionality reduction, association rules, regression and classification, big data tools, and the ethics and storytelling that make results usable. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory data science course.
modelledOn: Adhikari, DeNero and Wagner, Computational and Inferential Thinking: The Foundations of Data Science
Wickham, Cetinkaya-Rundel and Grolemund, R for Data Science
Provost and Fawcett, Data Science for Business
outcomes: Describe the data science life cycle and plan a project from question to deployed insight.
Use Python and R to load, clean, transform, blend and summarise data from files, databases, APIs and the web.
Design a simple data warehouse and build business intelligence dashboards.
Create honest, effective visualisations and communicate findings as a data story.
Apply clustering, PCA, association rules, regression and classification with proper validation.
Process data at scale with distributed tools and handle privacy and ethics responsibly.

units.title: Introduction to data science and the project life cycle
topics: What data science is: statistics, computing and domain knowledge; roles in a data team
The life cycle: question, acquire, clean, explore, model, evaluate, communicate, deploy, monitor (CRISP-DM)
Data types and sources: structured, semi-structured, unstructured; open data from the Ghana Statistical Service and the World Bank
Framing business and research questions; defining success metrics
Reproducible work: notebooks, scripts, version control, environments

units.title: R and Python for data
topics: Python: NumPy arrays, pandas DataFrames, indexing, grouping, merging, reshaping
R: vectors, data frames, the tidyverse (dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2)
Reading and writing CSV, Excel, JSON, SQL; dates and times; text and regular expressions
Exploratory data analysis: summaries, distributions, outliers, missing data
Choosing between R and Python and moving between them

units.title: Data collection and blending
topics: Collecting data: surveys, sensors, logs, APIs, web scraping (ethically and legally)
Data cleaning: types, duplicates, inconsistent categories, missing values and imputation, outliers
Blending sources: joins, entity resolution, fuzzy matching, unit and currency harmonisation
Data quality assessment and documentation (data dictionaries, provenance)

units.title: Business intelligence and data warehousing
topics: OLTP versus OLAP; the data warehouse and data marts; ETL and ELT pipelines
Dimensional modelling: facts, dimensions, star and snowflake schemas
OLAP operations: slice, dice, roll-up, drill-down; SQL for analytics (window functions, CUBE)
Dashboards with Power BI, Tableau, Metabase or Superset; KPIs for a retail chain or a hospital

units.title: Data visualisation
topics: Principles: encoding, chart choice, colour, scales, small multiples, avoiding deception
matplotlib, seaborn, plotly and ggplot2; maps and geospatial plots of Ghana's regions
Interactive dashboards and notebooks
Critiquing charts from the press and government reports

units.title: Machine learning: regression and classification
topics: Supervised learning setup; train/validation/test splits; cross-validation; overfitting and regularisation
Linear and polynomial regression; logistic regression; k-nearest neighbours; decision trees and random forests; gradient boosting
Evaluation: RMSE, R-squared, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, confusion matrices, class imbalance
Feature engineering, encoding, scaling, pipelines in scikit-learn and tidymodels
Case: predicting loan default, crop yield or student dropout

units.title: Machine learning: clustering, PCA and association rules
topics: k-means, hierarchical and DBSCAN clustering; choosing k; interpreting clusters (customer segmentation)
Principal component analysis: variance, loadings, visualisation of high-dimensional data; t-SNE and UMAP in brief
Association rules: support, confidence, lift, Apriori and FP-growth; market basket analysis
Anomaly detection basics

units.title: Big data analytics
topics: The Vs of big data; when a laptop is not enough
Distributed storage and compute: HDFS, MapReduce, Spark DataFrames and MLlib; cloud data warehouses
Streaming analytics and real-time dashboards
Working with big data on a small budget: sampling, columnar formats (Parquet), DuckDB

units.title: Ethics, privacy and storytelling with data
topics: Privacy, consent, anonymisation and re-identification; Ghana's Data Protection Act and GDPR
Bias in data and models; fairness metrics; algorithmic accountability; responsible AI
Storytelling: narrative structure, audience, executive summaries, presenting uncertainty
Capstone: an end-to-end project on a local dataset with a dashboard, model and written story

schedule.title: What data science is and the project life cycle
schedule.exercise: Pick a local problem such as predicting market prices or school attendance, and write the question, data needed, success metric and the stages of the life cycle you would follow.

tasks.title: Load a small CSV of Ghana Statistical Service figures, list each column with its data type and say which are structured or semi-structured
Load a table of regional population data into the database engine and write three queries that answer a question a district planner might ask
Run a mini project from a raw file through cleaning, a simple model and a short written finding, labelling each step with its CRISP-DM phase

schedule.title: Framing questions and reproducible work
schedule.exercise: Rewrite three vague requests from a manager into precise, measurable data questions with a success metric and a data source for each.

tasks.title: Create a notebook that reads a dataset, prints its summary and is rerun from top to bottom, then fix a cell that depends on hidden state
Compare two candidate metrics for a loan-repayment question on the same data, and explain which one better matches the business goal
Put an analysis script under version control with a requirements file, make two commits, and show another user can reproduce the same output

schedule.title: Data wrangling in Python and R
schedule.exercise: Convert five common spreadsheet operations (filter, sort, group, join, pivot) into pandas and tidyverse code, and tabulate where the two differ.

tasks.title: Use pandas to filter rows, create a new column and compute group means on a school results table, and check the totals by hand
Read a CSV and a JSON file with different date formats, parse them into proper dates and merge them on a shared key
Reproduce a multi-step pandas pipeline in R with dplyr, then check both give identical results on a sales table of 1000 rows

schedule.title: Exploratory data analysis
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page exploratory report on a dataset of your choice, listing five observations, the evidence for each and the follow-up questions they raise.

tasks.title: Compute summary statistics and plot a histogram for each numeric column of a farm survey dataset, and note two outliers
Investigate missing values in a household survey, show their pattern across columns and test two imputation choices on a key statistic
Run the same exploration in Python and in R on one dataset and list every difference in output, defaults or syntax that surprised you

schedule.title: Collecting, cleaning and blending data
schedule.exercise: Write a data dictionary and a data quality log for a messy dataset, describing each column, its allowed values and every correction you made.

tasks.title: Clean a table with duplicate rows, inconsistent region spellings and text numbers, and report how many rows each fix changed
Join a customer table and a payments table with a SQL query, find customers without payments and reconcile the totals against a control figure
Match two lists of business names with spelling variations using fuzzy matching, choose a threshold and report precision and recall on a hand-labelled sample

schedule.title: Warehouses, dimensional models and dashboards
schedule.exercise: Design a star schema for a retail chain with sales, products, stores and dates, and list five business questions each table makes easy to answer.

tasks.title: Create fact and dimension tables for a pharmacy chain, load sample rows and write a query that totals sales by region and month
Write SQL with window functions to rank stores by monthly sales and compute a running total and the percentage change from the previous month
Build a KPI set for a hospital (bed occupancy, waiting time, readmissions) from a star schema and justify each chart choice for managers

schedule.title: Data visualisation
schedule.exercise: Find two misleading charts in a newspaper or report, state what is wrong with each, and redraw one honestly by hand.

tasks.title: Plot the same dataset as a bar, line and scatter chart, and choose which best shows a trend in rainfall by month
Draw a choropleth or bubble map of a regional indicator for Ghana from supplied data, with a clear legend and a colour-blind-safe palette
Take a flawed chart with a truncated axis and mixed scales, reproduce it, then correct it and explain every change in a caption

schedule.title: Supervised learning and evaluation
schedule.exercise: Explain with a worked example why accuracy is misleading on imbalanced data, and show how precision, recall and F1 give a fairer picture.

tasks.title: Split a dataset into training and test sets, fit a linear regression and compare training and test error to detect overfitting
Train a logistic regression and a decision tree on the same classification task and compare their confusion matrices on the held-out test set
Handle a 95 to 5 class imbalance in fraud data using resampling or class weights and report the change in recall and F1

schedule.title: Features, pipelines and a prediction case
schedule.exercise: Write a short plan for predicting crop yield or student dropout, listing candidate features, risks of bias and how you would evaluate the model.

tasks.title: Build a pipeline that imputes missing values, scales numeric columns and one-hot encodes categories, and fit it without data leakage
Predict loan default on a given dataset with a tuned random forest, report cross-validated metrics and name the three most important features
Compare gradient boosting with a simple baseline on a crop-yield prediction task, test the gain for significance and state when the simple model is preferable

schedule.title: Unsupervised learning
schedule.exercise: Describe how you would use clustering to segment customers of a mobile money agent network and how you would check that the segments are useful.

tasks.title: Run k-means with k from 2 to 8 on a customer dataset, plot the elbow curve and pick a k with a short justification
Apply PCA to a ten-feature dataset, plot the first two components coloured by class, and report the variance explained
Compute support, confidence and lift for item pairs in a market-basket table using SQL and keep the rules that exceed given thresholds

schedule.title: Big data and scaling
schedule.exercise: Estimate whether a given dataset (rows, columns, growth per month) fits on a laptop, and decide when a cloud warehouse or Spark would be justified.

tasks.title: Convert a large CSV into a columnar file, query it with an embedded analytical database and compare run time and file size with pandas
Run a word count as a map and reduce on a text file split into partitions and compare the result with a single-pass count
Set up a small cloud data warehouse and storage bucket, load a dataset, run a query and estimate monthly cost in cedis for three usage levels

schedule.title: Ethics, privacy and fairness
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page privacy impact note for a project that uses hospital records, covering consent, anonymisation, re-identification risk and who may access the data.

tasks.title: Remove names and ids from a patient table, then show how date of birth, postcode and sex can still re-identify rows, and measure k-anonymity
Compute approval rates and error rates by gender and region for a given loan model and state whether the gap breaches a fairness threshold
Reduce a measured fairness gap in a loan model by reweighting or thresholds, and report the accuracy cost of the improvement

schedule.title: Storytelling and capstone
schedule.exercise: Prepare a five-minute presentation with a one-slide executive summary of your capstone, aimed at a district officer who is not a data specialist.

tasks.title: Write an executive summary and one annotated chart that communicates a finding and its uncertainty from a given analysis in under 150 words
Load a local dataset into the database engine, design a star schema and write the queries that feed three dashboard indicators for the capstone
Complete an end-to-end project on a local dataset with cleaning, model, evaluation, a dashboard and a short narrative, all runnable from one notebook
